subject: Logic
title: The Prisoner's Dilemma
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Prisoner's Dilemma.

hook.text: Two suspects are interrogated separately. Each can betray the other for freedom—or stay silent and risk everything.

buildup.text: If both cooperate, they get light sentences. If both betray, heavy sentences. If one betrays, they go free.

discovery.text: Rational self-interest says always betray—but mutual betrayal is worse for both than mutual cooperation.

twist.text: In repeated games, cooperation can emerge through tit-for-tat: cooperate first, then mirror your opponent.

climax.text: The dilemma reveals why trust, reputation, and long-term relationships are essential for collective well-being.

punchline.text: Rational for each. Terrible for both.

quiz.question: What is the core tension of the prisoner's dilemma?
options: Individual rationality leads to a worse outcome than cooperation
Betrayal is always the best strategy
